I will keep things simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest path for me is still the usual wheat and summer maize rotation, because I know how to manage it, the land suits it, and it spreads my risk across the year. At my age, I do not want to chase crops that need too much hand labor or market guessing. I will put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize. If I have a small piece of lighter land, I may use a little of it for peanuts, but my main plan is grain. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and a harvest I can count on. I will fertilize in a moderate way, not too heavy, because that wastes money and can make the crop lodge. I will rely on a few key irrigations at the important growth stages, especially for wheat at overwintering, jointing, and filling if water is available, and for maize around seeding and big flare stages if the rain is short. I will not spray too much; I will only do the few necessary pesticide applications when weeds, insects, or disease become a real problem. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage and fits my machinery and habits. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a stable yield, lower labor pressure, and less risk.
